content.summary: The fragile split-completion step withstands adversarial inspection. Merely requiring completions to intersect would be insufficient: a five-completion local counterexample exists. The manuscript and formal source correctly add the shared high-star obstructions, which force intersection in each coordinate and yield the cap four. I also checked the common-extension-point argument for a potential non-Helly triangle of extension pairs; its mass inequalities exclude that alternative.

findings.statement: Pairwise intersection of the residual completions alone does not imply the claimed four-completion cap; the actual-family star membership hypotheses are essential and are present in both Section 4.2 and the formal statement.
findings.disposition: No repair required. Preserve the explicit high-star argument when editing the proof.

checks.method: Read CompletionCompatibility.lean and TenLinkIntersection.lean; independently reconstruct the cases in Section 4.2. Run scratch/alpha/round03_split_check.py using the canonical ten-design from frozen source.
checks.observation: For 25 local completions and all 300 pairs, absence of a sunflower with the fixed row or a high-star member agrees exactly with intersection in both coordinates; the resulting compatibility graph has maximum clique four. Fixing one coordinate and using all five opposite edges gives five pairwise-intersecting completions, exposing why the shared-star hypotheses matter. The generic proof covers disjoint, equal, and singleton-intersecting coordinate edges and ensures the added star member is distinct via its center. The computation is a local diagnostic only, not a universal normalization argument.

checks.method: Read GenericHeavyExtensions.lean and rederive the mass concentration step without assuming pairwise-intersection implies a common point.
checks.observation: A chosen extension pair with weight at least nine has an endpoint of integer weight at least five. A heavy pair omitting it would force total weight at least fourteen, contradicting the total cap ten. This excludes the potential triangle of pairwise-intersecting pairs with empty common intersection. The key-to-block map is injective because the shared extension point is excluded from every key.
